highlights.title: RAG-Safety-Bench: Reliable Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented LLM Safety
highlights.summary: RAG-Safety-Bench is a benchmark that isolates retrieval quality and evaluates the safety impact of retrieval‑augmented generation on LLMs across four distinct conditions.
highlights.detail: The benchmark separates non‑RAG, oracle‑document RAG, related‑document RAG, and a control setting, allowing researchers to pinpoint how retrieved content influences harmful outputs. It removes confounding retriever performance to focus purely on safety effects.

highlights.title: MindTopo: Can Foundation Models Reason in Topological Space?
highlights.summary: MindTopo is a benchmark that tests foundation models on topological reasoning, covering five properties at two cognitive levels with 11,030 instances across 13 task types.
highlights.detail: Tasks probe continuity, separation, order, enclosure, and knots, each evaluated for basic identification and for predicting changes. The dataset is procedurally generated, enabling controlled difficulty scaling and systematic analysis of spatial intuition beyond metric relations.

highlights.title: SpecGuard: Inference-Time Backdoor Detection For Free
highlights.summary: SpecGuard detects backdoors during LLM inference at zero added computation by repurposing speculative decoding.
highlights.detail: Speculative decoding runs a small draft model to propose tokens while the target model verifies them; SpecGuard monitors discrepancies to flag potential trigger activation without extra forward passes, preserving latency‑sensitive serving pipelines.

highlights.title: Lara Croft on a Microcontroller
highlights.summary: Hackaday’s “Lara Croft on a Microcontroller” article shows how modern microcontrollers now have enough horsepower to run complex demos that previously required careful resource budgeting.
highlights.detail: The piece highlights advances in MCU clock speeds, memory, and peripheral integration, enabling developers to implement graphics‑intensive projects without external co‑processors.

highlights.title: Taming Bitwise Behavior in GPU Kernels with Tensor Core: Black-Box Reconstruction, Compiler Enforcement, and Static Verification
highlights.summary: The arXiv paper shows that preserving a fixed reduction order in GPU kernels can incur up to 20 % performance loss, and it characterizes the bitwise‑behavior factors of reductions and GEMM.
highlights.detail: Factors include floating‑point reduction order, partial‑sum precision, fused multiply‑add usage, and rounding placement. Autotuners cannot reliably detect bitwise‑equivalent configurations, complicating reproducibility guarantees.

items.title: Now everyone can put data to work
items.summary: OpenAI introduced a Data agent in ChatGPT Work that lets users connect corporate data sources and build AI‑driven interactive dashboards via natural language.
items.detail: The agent can query structured tables, generate visualizations, and answer ad‑hoc questions, streamlining data analysis for non‑technical users while keeping data within the organization’s security perimeter.

items.title: Training a 3.8B LLM to 0.384 CORE for $998
items.summary: A 3.8 billion‑parameter LLM was trained to achieve 0.384 CORE performance for a total cost of $998.
items.detail: The result demonstrates that high‑capacity models can be trained on modest cloud credits, using efficient data pipelines and mixed‑precision techniques to keep compute expenses low.

items.title: Expanding AI access and cyber defense for federal, state, local, and tribal governments
items.summary: OpenAI and the GSA will provide eligible federal, state, local, and tribal governments with zero license fees, a 50% usage discount, and expanded cyber‑defense support for AI services.
items.detail: The program aims to broaden AI adoption in public sectors while mitigating security risks, offering dedicated threat monitoring and incident response resources alongside the pricing incentives.

items.title: How a researcher uses Codex and ChatGPT to search for new antimicrobial molecules
items.summary: César de la Fuente’s laboratory uses Codex and ChatGPT to scan both living and extinct genomes for antimicrobial candidates against drug‑resistant infections.
items.detail: The workflow combines large‑language‑model code generation with bioinformatics pipelines, accelerating the identification of novel peptide sequences that can be synthesized and tested for activity.

items.title: Model: WarmBloodAban/Minimax-h3_Singularity
items.summary: The WarmBloodAban/Minimax-h3_Singularity model, an image‑to‑video generator on Hugging Face, has been downloaded 96,682 times and received 267 likes.
items.detail: Its popularity reflects growing interest in generative video capabilities, and the model is licensed under a permissive open‑source agreement, enabling easy integration into multimedia projects.

items.title: Model: nex-agi/Nex-N2.5-Pro
items.summary: The Nex‑N2.5‑Pro text‑generation model on Hugging Face has recorded 3 downloads and 586 likes.
items.detail: Despite low download count, the model’s high like ratio suggests niche appreciation, possibly for its specialized architecture or fine‑tuned domain performance.

items.title: Model: nex-agi/Nex-N2.5-mini
items.summary: The Nex‑N2.5‑mini text‑generation model on Hugging Face has amassed 2,444 downloads and 664 likes.
items.detail: Its broader adoption indicates a balance of performance and resource efficiency, making it suitable for applications on modest hardware while maintaining quality outputs.

items.title: Security updates for Thursday
items.summary: LWN reports Thursday security updates across several Linux distributions, patching dozens of packages including kernels, libraries, and applications.
items.detail: Updates span AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle Linux, Slackware, and SUSE, addressing vulnerabilities in components such as OpenSSL, glibc, and the Linux kernel to improve system integrity.

items.title: Forgejo 16.0.4 and 15.0.8 address critical security vulnerability
items.summary: Forgejo released versions 16.0.4 and 15.0.8 fixing a critical remote‑code‑execution flaw in template‑repository handling.
items.detail: The vulnerability allowed a malicious template to recreate a .git folder during variable expansion, letting the host execute arbitrary code. The fix removes any .git directory after expansion, eliminating the attack path.

items.title: Julia 1.13 released
items.summary: Julia 1.13 was released, bringing faster package precompilation, REPL enhancements, and a graphical Juliaup version‑manager interface.
items.detail: The release notes list numerous performance and usability improvements; Juliaup provides a GUI for managing multiple Julia installations. LWN previously covered Julia 1.12 in November 2025.

items.title: [$] PostgreSQL 19's "scary patch contest"
items.summary: PostgreSQL 19’s September release is delayed after a “scary patch contest” email on August 25 highlighted numerous bug‑fix‑heavy patches, prompting an extra beta for additional testing.
items.detail: Contributor Robert Haas warned that several patches required unusually many fixes, leading to a revert of one patch and heavy revision of others. The added beta aims to ensure stability before the final launch.

items.title: 3D Imaging Without a Lens
items.summary: Hackaday explores lensless 3D imaging methods that capture depth without traditional camera optics.
items.detail: The article surveys unconventional hardware setups and mathematical techniques that reconstruct three‑dimensional scenes without lenses, highlighting potential low‑cost applications.

items.title: A Model-Centric DevOps Architecture for DEVS-Based Digital Twin Simulation Services
items.summary: A new DevOps architecture treats DEVS‑based digital‑twin models as first‑class artifacts defined in YAML, enabling validation, immutable versioning, and CI/CD deployment on Kubernetes.
items.detail: Models are validated structurally and semantically in pipelines, producing immutable identifiers for rollback. The platform runs as containerised microservices with state externalisation to support cloud‑native lifecycle management.

items.title: Rethinking Sparse Formats for RISC-V: A Hierarchical Approach to High-Performance SpMV
items.summary: The study introduces Hierarchical CSR, a modified sparse matrix format that, together with optimal format selection, yields an average 1.6× speedup for SpMV on RISC‑V boards.
items.detail: Implementations use RVV 1.0 intrinsics and are released as the open‑source C++ library RVVLASparse. Benchmarks on SpacemiT K1 and K3 boards show the benefit of format choice and the HCSR improvement.

items.title: Can AI Remediate Backend Failures Safely? GuardedAct with Blast-Radius-Aware Sandboxing
items.summary: GuardedAct adds a sandbox‑first, blast‑radius‑aware verification layer before executing LLM‑generated remediation actions, auto‑running only low‑risk fixes in production.
items.detail: The framework ingests diagnosis reports, prompts an LLM for candidate actions, simulates each in a digital‑twin sandbox to assess blast radius, and enforces a rollback‑confidence gate, escalating high‑risk actions for human review.

items.title: EMMI: Edge Multi-Modal Intelligence for Communication-Efficient MLLM Inference via Fused Representation Compression
items.summary: EMMI compresses modality‑specific edge representations into a compact latent vector, allowing communication‑efficient inference of multimodal large language models on constrained edge devices.
items.detail: Edge devices perform modality encoding, cross‑modal fusion, and learned compression before sending the latent representation to a server, reducing bandwidth while preserving inference quality.

items.title: Entwine: Coordinating Tiled Computation and Fine-Grained Communication across GPUs
items.summary: Entwine synchronizes tile computation order with fine‑grained SM‑based communication on GPUs, smoothing data flow to lower overall execution time.
items.detail: By reordering tile execution to produce data at a regular pace and coupling it with SM‑level communication, Entwine reduces stalls and resource contention, improving overall kernel completion time.

items.title: alsk1992/CloddsBot
items.summary: CloddsBot is an open‑source AI trading agent that operates autonomously across over 1,000 markets on multiple EVM chains and other platforms, self‑hosted and built on Claude.
items.detail: The bot scans for edge opportunities, executes instantly, manages risk, and supports a machine‑to‑machine payment protocol, allowing users to run it on their own infrastructure.

items.title: ast-grep/ast-grep
items.summary: ast‑grep is a Rust‑written CLI tool for structural code search, linting, and automated rewriting.
items.detail: It enables developers to query abstract syntax trees directly from the command line, facilitating precise refactoring and custom lint rules with high performance.

items.title: google-ai-edge/LiteRT-LM
items.summary: LiteRT‑LM is an open‑source inference framework from Google that enables production‑ready, high‑performance deployment of large language models on edge devices.
items.detail: Designed for edge environments, LiteRT‑LM provides optimized kernels and a small binary footprint to keep latency and memory usage low. It supports loading models converted to a compatible format and can be integrated into custom applications. Being open‑source, developers can extend or modify the inference pipeline for specific hardware.

items.title: vercel-labs/skills
items.summary: skills is an open‑source tool from Vercel Labs that offers a command‑line interface (npx skills) for creating and managing agent capabilities.
items.detail: The skills tool packages agent capabilities as modular, reusable components that can be installed and executed directly via npx without prior installation. Distributed through npm, it streamlines experimentation with AI agents by handling setup and execution from the command line.

items.title: JustVugg/colibri
items.summary: colibri is a pure‑C inference engine that runs frontier mixture‑of‑experts (MoE) models on existing hardware by streaming expert weights from disk without external dependencies.
items.detail: colibri’s engine is written entirely in C and avoids external libraries, enabling deployment on a wide range of systems. By streaming expert parameters from disk, it reduces RAM requirements, allowing large MoE models to run on commodity hardware.

items.title: NVIDIA/Megatron-LM
items.summary: Megatron‑LM is NVIDIA’s open‑source Python library for large‑scale training of transformer models, supporting research into scaling up model size and data.
items.detail: Megatron‑LM provides a scalable training framework that leverages model parallelism and pipeline parallelism to handle extremely large transformer models. The library includes utilities for efficient data loading, mixed‑precision training, and checkpointing, facilitating research into scaling trends.
